Turn 1 of 4 — read-back. Do not write any program JSON in this turn.

You are going to turn a run-of-show into a Rhylthyme program: parallel **tracks** of sequential **steps**, each with a duration and a start trigger, that one person follows against a live clock.

Plan this as a Rhylthyme run-of-show and deliver a live timeline: Wedding Reception Run Sheet — Ashgrove Barn for 90 guests, three courses
Resource limits: one kitchen pass, one bar, one microphone, two servers on the floor, one dance floor.
Everything must be finished by band's last set.

Source text (read all of it):
<<<
Wedding Reception Run Sheet — Ashgrove Barn, 90 guests

The ceremony breaks at four o'clock and this sheet starts there. One kitchen pass, one bar, one microphone, two servers on the floor, one band. The planner owns the room call; the MC owns everything that goes through the microphone. Nothing on the pass overlaps: the kitchen plates one course at a time and the floor waits for it.

Room
Flip the ceremony room to reception seating: 45 minutes, chairs out, rounds in, linen on.
Dress the tables with centrepieces, place cards and candles; 15 minutes once the flip is done.
Seat the guests when the planner calls the room; 15 minutes to get 90 people down.

Foyer
Open the bar as soon as the ceremony breaks; 20 minutes to set and pour the first round.
Pass canapes in the foyer from twenty minutes in, and keep passing for forty minutes to an hour, however long the photographs take.
Call the room to dinner once the canapes are done; 5 minutes.

Kitchen
Starters plate up fifteen minutes after the room starts seating; 15 minutes on the pass.
Mains go on the pass five minutes after the starter plates are cleared; 30 minutes.
Dessert plates up the moment the cake is cut; 15 minutes.

Floor
Serve the starters; 10 minutes.
Clear the starters twenty minutes after they go out; 10 minutes.
Serve the mains; 15 minutes.
Clear the mains forty minutes after they go out; 10 minutes.
Serve the dessert; 10 minutes.

Programme
Welcome toast as soon as the guests are seated; 5 minutes on the microphone.
First dance once the main plates are cleared; 5 minutes.
Speeches when the MC cues them: two or three of them, fifteen minutes total, twenty-five at the outside.
Cut the cake straight after the speeches; 10 minutes.
Dancing starts ten minutes after the dessert is served and runs until the band's last set.

Notes for the day
The photographs are the only thing we do not control, so the canape window is the slack in the sheet: if the couple are late back from the orchard the bar carries it. Everything downstream of the room call is fixed. If the speeches run long, the kitchen holds the dessert rather than plating it early — the pass is the bottleneck and a plated dessert sitting under a lamp is worse than a five minute gap on the floor.
>>>

Read all of it before you answer. Then say back, in one paragraph and in your own words: what is being made, for how many (or at what scale), by when, and under what constraints — equipment that exists only once, how many people are working, anything that has to be held, rested or ready at a particular moment. If the text you were given looks truncated, or points at a section that is not here, say so instead of filling the gap.

End your reply with the same read-back as JSON in a single ```json fenced block:

```json
{
  "summary": "one paragraph: what is being made, for how many, by when, under what constraints",
  "servesOrScale": "8 people",
  "deadline": "2026-11-26T18:00:00",
  "constraints": ["one oven", "two burners", "two cooks"]
}
```

**Read-back**

This is a wedding reception run sheet for 90 guests at Ashgrove Barn, covering three courses, and it starts on one clock at the moment the ceremony breaks — four o'clock — not at the ceremony itself. Work splits across four parallel crews hanging off that moment: the room (flip the ceremony space to rounds, dress the tables, seat 90 people), the foyer (open the bar and pour a first round, then pass canapes), the kitchen pass (plates starters, then mains, then dessert — one course at a time, never overlapping), and the floor (two servers serving and clearing each course), with the MC’s programme — welcome toast, first dance, speeches, cake cut, then dancing — riding on top of all of it. The single-instance things are the real shape of the day: one kitchen pass, one bar, one microphone, one dance floor, and one band, plus exactly two servers on the floor, so the floor is the second bottleneck after the pass. Two things are explicitly *held* rather than worked early: the dessert is not plated until the cake is cut, and if the speeches run long the kitchen holds it back rather than let a plated dessert sit under a lamp — a five-minute gap on the floor beats that. The only genuine slack in the sheet is the canape window (starting 20 minutes in, lasting 40 to 60 minutes depending on how long the photographs take); everything downstream of the room call is fixed. Two gaps I won’t invent: the sheet says everything must be finished by the band’s last set but never gives a clock time for it, and it never says how many people are in the kitchen or on the room crew (only that there are two servers, one planner and an MC). The speech block is likewise a range, 15 minutes nominal and 25 at the outside.

```json
{
  "summary": "A wedding reception run-of-show for 90 guests at Ashgrove Barn, three courses, on one clock starting when the ceremony breaks at 16:00. Parallel lanes: the room (45 min flip to rounds, 15 min dressing, 15 min seating 90), the foyer (bar opens at the break, 20 min to first round; canapes pass from 20 min in for 40-60 min while photographs run; 5 min call to dinner), the kitchen pass (starters 15 min, 15 min after seating starts; mains 30 min, 5 min after starters are cleared; dessert 15 min, plated the moment the cake is cut), the floor (two servers serving and clearing each course), and the MC's programme (5 min welcome toast once seated, 5 min first dance once mains are cleared, 15-25 min of speeches, 10 min cake cut, then dancing from 10 min after dessert until the band's last set). Single-instance resources: one kitchen pass that never overlaps, one bar, one microphone, one dance floor, one band, and two servers on the floor. Held, not plated early: dessert waits for the cake cut and is held back if speeches overrun. The canape window is the only slack; everything downstream of the room call is fixed. Finish is the band's last set, but the sheet gives no clock time for it, and kitchen/room crew sizes are not stated.",
  "servesOrScale": "90 guests, three courses",
  "deadline": "the band's last set — no clock time given in the sheet (must be supplied; start anchor is 16:00 when the ceremony breaks)",
  "constraints": [
    "one kitchen pass — no two courses plate at once, one course at a time",
    "one bar",
    "one microphone — the MC owns everything that goes through it (welcome toast, speeches)",
    "two servers on the floor (serve and clear each course)",
    "one dance floor",
    "one band — dancing runs until its last set, which is the hard finish",
    "room flip, dressing and seating are sequential on the planner's room call",
    "canape passing (from 20 min in, 40-60 min) is the only slack and absorbs photographic overrun",
    "dessert must not be plated early — it waits on the cake cut, and is held back if speeches overrun",
    "everything downstream of the room call to dinner is fixed"
  ]
}
```

**The model, restated**

A **track** is one sequential line of work — one station, one crew, one performer — and its steps run one after another and never overlap; anything that has to happen *while* another step is running gets its own track alongside it. Every **step** carries exactly one duration kind: `fixed` (`seconds`, or a string like `"15m"`), `variable` (`minSeconds` / `maxSeconds`, plus a `defaultSeconds` so previews have something to plan against), or `indefinite` (it runs until the person ends it). A **startTrigger** is how a step joins the clock: `programStart` at t=0, `programStartOffset` for "twenty minutes in", `afterStep` / `afterStepWithBuffer` to chain off another step starting or ending (with an optional offset or buffer), `manual` for a human tap, `onAbort` for a cancellation path, and `compound` to wait for all or any of several triggers. **`stepId`s are unique across the whole program**, not per track, so every `afterStep` reference is unambiguous and a track's order is expressed by each step pointing back at its predecessor. Every **`task`** a step occupies — pass, bar, mic, dance floor — needs a matching `resourceConstraints` entry, and that entry's `maxConcurrent` is the hard cap that stops two steps claiming something the barn only has one of. Repeated work is **`replicates: { count: n, mode: "serial" | "parallel" | "stagger" }`** on a single step, never n copied steps: per-instance follow-on work chains with `instances: "each"`, the step that waits for the lot uses `instances: "all"`, and `replicates.maxInFlight: k` holds the upstream step back when the holding area between them only fits k.

**What this run-of-show will constrain**

Six things exist in single or limited supply here and each becomes one `task` with its own cap. The **kitchen pass** is `maxConcurrent: 1` — the sheet is explicit that nothing on the pass overlaps and one course plates at a time, so starters, mains and dessert can never run together. The **bar** is `1`. The **microphone** is `1` — the MC owns it, so the welcome toast and the speeches are serialised against each other through that one channel. The **floor** is `2`, because there are exactly two servers: serving and clearing a course, and passing canapés, all draw on the same two pairs of hands. The **dance floor** is `1`, covering the first dance and then the open dancing. The **room** is `1` — the planner's room call, covering the flip, the dressing, the seating and the call to dinner, and they are sequential anyway, but the entry keeps the room call from being double-booked. Two resources I am deliberately *not* declaring as tasks: the **band**, which is not occupied by any step in the sheet so much as it *is* the deadline ("until the band's last set"), and the **kitchen brigade**, whose size the sheet never states — it's the pass they're working at, and the pass is what I'm capping.

On people: the sheet names exactly four roles — one planner, one MC, two servers on the floor — so I'll declare `actors: 4` as the floor-visible minimum. The kitchen crew size is genuinely not in the text, so I'm not inventing a number for it; if you want kitchen staff counted as actors, tell me how many and I'll raise it.

```json
{
  "acknowledgement": "A track is one sequential line of work — steps in it never overlap, and anything happening concurrently with it needs its own track. Each step has exactly one duration kind: fixed (seconds), variable (min/max + default) or indefinite. A startTrigger attaches the step to the clock or to another step: programStart, programStartOffset, afterStep, afterStepWithBuffer, manual, onAbort, compound. stepIds are unique across the whole program, not per track, so afterStep references are unambiguous. Every task a step occupies needs a matching resourceConstraints entry, and maxConcurrent is what stops two steps sharing the one pass, the one bar or the one microphone. Repeated work is replicates {count, mode} on ONE step — never copies — chained per instance with instances: 'each', joined with 'all', and bounded by maxInFlight when the holding area between them only fits k.",
  "resourceConstraints": [
    { "task": "pass", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "bar", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "mic", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "floor", "maxConcurrent": 2 },
    { "task": "danceFloor", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "room", "maxConcurrent": 1 }
  ],
  "actors": 4
}
```

**Two judgement calls, flagged rather than hidden.** The sheet says the planner owns the room call and the MC owns the microphone, and "Call the room to dinner" sits in the Foyer section as a 5-minute call — I've given it `task: "room"` (it is the planner's room call, not an MC mic moment); if you'd rather it went through the mic, move it to `"mic"`. "Cut the cake" is a 10-minute floor-centre moment with nothing else running in the middle of the room, so I've given it `task: "danceFloor"` — that also serialises it against the first dance and the open dancing, which the venue's one dance floor physically demands.

**The speeches are a bundle I have not split.** "two or three of them, fifteen minutes total, twenty-five at the outside" could become `replicates: {count: 3}` of ~5 minutes each, but the count itself is a range and the run sheet only ever budgets the block as a whole, so I've kept it as one `variable` step at 15–25 minutes.

**One inferred step:** a microphone check before the toast. One mic, an MC, 90 guests — the sheet never says it, but nothing in the Programme is possible without it. That is the only preheat/thaw/rest-class gap I think the work actually has; I have not invented a kitchen canapé-prep step, because the sheet treats canapés as ready to pass.

**Still missing from the text:** any clock time for the band's last set, which is the stated finish for the whole day. That comes from you in turn 4 as a `finishAt`.
